fatal_errors: The proposed SFE-tuning strategy does not reconstruct the target high-energy ball milling followed by spark plasma sintering method.
No target processing conditions, including milling speed, ball-to-powder ratio, milling duration, SPS temperature, heating rate, or hold time, are identified.
The stated mechanism lists investigative tools rather than a causal mechanism and omits grain-boundary, dislocation, and solid-solution strengthening.

The cited evidence supports links between SFE and deformation modes in mainly FCC HEAs, but does not establish the broad claim that SFE tuning itself refines microstructure or produces the target FCC/BCC nanocrystalline structure.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses HEA phase stability and mechanical-property optimization, so it is thematically aligned and scientifically plausible as an alternative strategy. Evidence E4 and E5 support the influence of SFE on slip, twinning, and martensitic transformation. However, it misses the target material, powder-processing route, quantitative process window, mixed 83% FCC/17% BCC structure, sub-48 nm grains, densification mechanism, and measured hardness and strength. The baseline and boundaries are placeholders, while the proposed falsification experiment is directionally useful but lacks compositions, processing controls, SFE measurement methods, and quantitative acceptance thresholds. Several cited items are irrelevant to the central SFE claim.
